Consult Summary:
- Teleconsult for sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual disturbance, dizziness, and vomiting; clinician impression: likely migraine; advised OTC ibuprofen plus antiemetic and same-day in-person neurological assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset headache starting this morning (~4 hours before consult), left-sided, intensity ~6/10, worsened by movement; cannot tolerate screens.
- Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with zigzag lines; dizziness; nausea; vomited twice. Paracetamol taken ~3 hours after onset with no relief.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar headaches; denies limb weakness; gait normal. Denies known drug allergies. No regular medications. Unlikely pregnant.
- Past medical history: Previous kidney stones.
- Family history: Mother has migraines; family history of hypothyroidism.
- Social history and preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Suspected migraine (first episode) with visual aura and associated nausea/vomiting. Plan for in-person neurological exam to exclude other causes.

Plan:
- Medications: 
  - Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Anti-sickness medication from pharmacy (agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Advise sugary, carbonated drink (e.g., cola).
- Follow-up:
  - Arrange same-day, in-person appointment for full neurological examination.
  - If symptoms substantially improve before the appointment, patient may cancel; otherwise attend as planned.
  - Contact clinic if any further problems before the appointment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; focused neurological exam; fundoscopy; blood pressure; detailed red-flag screen (e.g., neck stiffness/fever, worst-ever thunderclap onset, head trauma, anticoagulant use); pregnancy test/LMP; medication doses and specific antiemetic; comprehensive allergy review; social history (tobacco/alcohol); headache triggers and prior headache history beyond this episode.
- Internal conflicts: Family thyroid history—clinician said “hyperthyroid,” patient clarified “hypothyroidism” (conflict noted; patient reports hypothyroidism in family).
- Transcript quality: Minor connection issues and occasional unclear phrasing; overall adequate to determine clinical details.
